title: Portrayal lab (v1) - library devices placed in one rack, and the links between them
description: A LAB IS A RACK ELEVATION PLUS A LINK LIST. It lives at labs/<name>/lab.yaml, names library devices by their `name`, and names ports by placement id; nothing about geometry lives here, because a viewer resolves port positions from the compiled drawings. The build checks every placement (L139-L143, L153, L154) and writes each one to labs.json with its position resolved: the absolute rack unit, the face and the host. Rack units count the way the rack counts, U1 at the bottom, and a placement's `ru` is the lowest unit it takes.

name.description: the lab's id, by convention its directory

title.description: the heading a viewer shows; omitted means `name`

provenance.description: where each part of the lab came from, one sentence per topic - the layout, the topology, what was assumed

rack.description: the frame. A viewer may read keys beyond these two, so others are allowed

height-ru.description: rack units in the frame; omitted means 42. Every placement fits inside it (L142)

rails-only.description: draw the rails without a cabinet round them

devices.description: the placements, one per device in the rack

links.description: the cables. Each end is [placement id, port id] or [placement id, port id, strand]

placement.description: ONE DEVICE IN THE RACK. A `rack` device is placed by `ru`. A `rack-face` part - one that bolts to the rail face over a rack unit it shares, docs/cable-managers-design.md section 6 - is placed on a host (`on`, with `unit`) or at a rack unit (`ru`), never both, and says which `face`; one narrower than the rack opening may say which `side` of it. A `rack-side` part - one that stands beside the rack on the side of an upright, docs/vertical-cable-managers-design.md section 3.5 - says which `side`, and is placed by `ru`, its bottom unit (default 1), on a `face`. `on` and `unit` are for rack-face parts only, `face` for rack-face and rack-side parts (L140, L153).

id.description: unique in the lab (L139); `on` and every link end name a placement by it

cfg.description: which of the device's configurations; omitted means its default (L139)

ru.description: the lowest rack unit the device takes, U1 at the bottom of the rack (L142); for a rack-side part the unit it starts beside, omitted meaning 1 (L154)

face.description: rack-face and rack-side parts only: the rail face it bolts to, or the face a rack-side part's working side looks out of. Omitted means front. On the rear it is behind the rear rails and turned round

side.description: which side of the rack, seen from the front. A `rack-side` part states it: the upright it stands beside (L153). A `rack-face` part narrower than the rack opening may: the rail it bolts to, so that one on each rail shares a rack unit and a face (L142, L153). Omitted on a rack-face part means it takes the whole unit on its face

on.description: rack-face parts only: the id of the rack device it sits in front of (or behind), so that it moves with that device (L139, L141)

unit.description: rack-face parts placed `on` a host only: which of the host's rack units, counted the way the rack counts - 1 is the host's bottom unit. Omitted means 1. Several parts on one tall host are several placements with different `unit` values (L141)

turned.description: the device is racked back to front: its other panel faces out of the face it is mounted to

span.description: a name for the run, so a viewer can colour spans apart
